The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 623197ae012dfb0c), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 12. statement: Keep the dimensions of Theorem 3.1. Let ν ≤ Hσ, H < ∞, be a probability measure. Let S ∼ ν and X ∼ γm be independent, let W be countable with H(W) < ∞ and any joint law with (S, X), and let Z ∼ γr be independent of (S, X, W). Put G = (X; Z) and Y = GS. For every positive-probability w, let ρw ≪ σ be a finite nonnegative measure satisfying (9) with constants Bw, Dw > 0, and set Cw = eCd Bw ( 1 + log+ (Dw/Bw) ) , where C is the constant in the theorem. Assume E log(1 + CW ) < ∞. The actual conditional law of Y given (G, W) has a Lebesgue density. With the versions (3), pρW ,1/j(G, Y ) −→ pρW (G, Y ) almost surely under the actual law. For every δ > 0, and also for the exact density, E log ( 1 + pρW ,δ(G, Y ) ) ≤ I(X; W | S) q + E log(1 + CW ), (15) E log ( 1 + pρW (G, Y ) ) ≤ I(X; W | S) q + E log(1 + CW ) ≤ H(W) q + E log(1 + CW ). (16) In particular log+ pρW (G, Y ) is integrable, and the extended expectation of log pρW (G, Y ), with log 0 = −∞, is defined and bounded above by the same right-hand side. For a deterministic countable refinement W′ = (W, E(S, W)) of finite entropy, the row charge is unchanged: I(X; W′ | S) = I(X; W | S).
